+**Two bugs recur in hand-written conditional fillers — `fill_template.py` avoids both,
+and you MUST avoid them if you write your own:**
+1. **A kept block's inner placeholders must ALSO be replaced.** When `{{IF_X}}` is
+   included, every `{{KEY}}` between the markers still needs its value substituted.
+   Leaving them raw is the most common failure (e.g. an offer letter that keeps the
+   relocation clause but prints a literal `{{RELOCATION_AMOUNT}}`).
+2. **The gate key is often NOT the tag name.** `{{IF_RELOCATION}}` may be gated by a
+   data field named `RELOCATION_PACKAGE` (= "Yes"/"No"), not `RELOCATION`. Look up the
+   include/exclude decision by exact key first, then by any data key that contains the
+   tag as a token; treat yes/true/1/y as include and no/false/0/n/none/"" as exclude.
+   Defaulting to INCLUDE when no gating field is found is safer than silently deleting a
+Blocks also frequently **span multiple paragraphs** (`{{IF_X}}` on one line, content in
+following paragraphs, `{{END_IF_X}}` later) — a single-paragraph-only scan misses these.
+`fill_template.py` tracks an include-stack across paragraphs to handle them.

+#### Comparing an extracted PDF table to a spreadsheet (data-diff)
+When a task asks you to compare a table extracted from a PDF against a
+spreadsheet/CSV and report which rows were **deleted / added / modified**, use the
+bundled helper `scripts/compare_tables.py` — do not re-derive the comparison:
+**Two mistakes make the "modified" count wrong. The helper handles both:**
+1. **Compare NORMALIZED values, never raw strings.** A cell pulled from a PDF is
+   always a string and numbers often keep a thousands separator or currency sign:
+   the same salary is `"112,000"` in the PDF but `112000` (int) in the spreadsheet.
+   A naive `str(old) != str(new)` then marks EVERY such cell "modified" — e.g.
+   **10495 false positives instead of the true 20**. Always canonicalize both sides
+   if normalize_cell(old) != normalize_cell(new):   # <- the line that flips the result
+   to `None`, and leaves genuine text as a stripped string — so only real changes remain.
+2. **Multi-page tables: read the header ONCE.** Continuation pages have no header row,
+   so building a DataFrame per page with `columns=table[0]` silently drops each
+   continuation page's first data row (undercounting rows and IDs). `extract_pdf_table`
+   reads the header once and keeps every row across all pages.
+keyed by the ID column (auto-detected if `key_col` is omitted). Rename those keys to match
